title: Closed immersions of algebraic spaces descend along fppf coverings
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\{Y_i\to Y\}_{i\in I}$ be a set-indexed jointly surjective family of flat locally finitely presented morphisms, with these properties tested on etale scheme charts [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-trf-algebraic-space-jointly-surjective-family]. Then $f$ is a closed immersion if and only if every $X\times_Y Y_i\to Y_i$ is a closed immersion. Here closed immersion means representable by schemes and a closed immersion on every scheme base change [def-weil-closed-immersion]; fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers].

source.place: Tag 0420, lemma-descending-property-closed-immersion (fpqc locality, specialized to fppf families)

proof.text: First suppose $f$ is a closed immersion. For a scheme $T\to Y_i$, the sheaf fibre products $(X\times_Y Y_i)\times_{Y_i}T$ and $X\times_YT$ are canonically identical: on test schemes the inverse maps forget, respectively insert, the prescribed $Y_i$ coordinate. By the definition of closed immersion for spaces, the latter is a scheme closed in $T$. This proves both representability and the closed-immersion property of each $f_i:X\times_Y Y_i\to Y_i$.

source.place: Tag 03M4 (lemma-closed-immersion-local), (1) implies (2), applied to arbitrary space base change

proof.text: Conversely suppose every $f_i$ is a closed immersion. For any affine scheme $V\to Y_i$, its pullback is a closed subscheme of $V$, hence affine by the affine-open characterization in [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Thus each $f_i$ is affine in the precise sense of [lem-sfb-space-four-property-fppf-descent], namely affine scheme source on every affine scheme test. Apply the affine clause of that node to the given set-indexed jointly surjective flat locally finitely presented family. It follows that $f$ is affine. This uses neither finite presentation of $f$ nor representability of $f$ in advance.

source.place: Tag 0420 (lemma-descending-property-closed-immersion): first descend affineness, using Tag 041Z (lemma-descending-property-affine)

proof.text: Fix an affine scheme $T$ and $t:T\to Y$. Affineness just obtained gives an affine scheme $E_T$ representing $X\times_YT$. Apply [lem-sfb-space-fppf-finite-affine-refinement] to the original covering and $t$. It gives finitely many affine schemes $V_j$, indices $a(j)$, and maps $p_j:V_j\to T$, $r_j:V_j\to Y_{a(j)}$ with $q_{a(j)}r_j=tp_j$; the $p_j$ are flat, locally finitely presented and jointly surjective. Accordingly $\{p_j\}$ is a scheme fppf covering by [def-pc-fppf-site], and is an fpqc covering by [lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc]. No individual $Y_i\to Y$ is assumed quasi-compact.

source.place: Tag 0DFQ (lemma-zariski-etale-smooth-syntomic-fppf-fpqc), proof: finite affine refinement; topologies.tex Tag 022C, scheme fppf implies fpqc

proof.text: For each $j$ the scheme $E_T\times_TV_j$ represents $X\times_YV_j$, and also represents $(X\times_YY_{a(j)})\times_{Y_{a(j)}}V_j$. The identifications preserve the projection to $V_j$: on test schemes each map forgets a coordinate fixed by the maps $p_j,r_j$, and its inverse inserts that coordinate. The hypothesis that $f_{a(j)}$ is a closed immersion therefore says exactly that $E_T\times_TV_j\to V_j$ is a closed immersion. Apply [lem-pc-fpqc-descend-closed-immersion] to the scheme morphism $E_T\to T$ and the fpqc family $\{p_j\}$. Hence $E_T\to T$ is a closed immersion for every affine scheme test $T\to Y$.

source.place: Tag 0420 (lemma-descending-property-closed-immersion), final reduction to descent.tex Tag 02L6 (lemma-descending-property-closed-immersion)

proof.text: Finally let $T\to Y$ be any scheme test. The base-change and scheme-target clauses of [lem-sfb-space-affine-locality], applied to the affine morphism $f$, show that $E=X\times_YT$ is represented by a scheme and $E\to T$ is affine. For every affine open $V\subseteq T$, its inverse image in $E$ is $X\times_YV$ over $V$, by the same fibre-product identity. The preceding step says this morphism is a closed immersion, so its source is affine and its map on affine sections is surjective. The affine-open characterization of [def-weil-closed-immersion] now says $E\to T$ is a closed immersion. As $T$ was arbitrary, this proves the required representability and closed immersion of $f$. Empty targets and empty covers are included: an empty jointly surjective family forces $Y$ to be empty, and the finite affine refinement permits $J=\varnothing$ over the empty affine test.

source.place: Tag 03WG (lemma-affine-local), Tag 03WI (lemma-base-change-affine); Tag 03M4 (lemma-closed-immersion-local), affine tests to scheme tests
